description: Dispatch an async job that reads current-day REST API consumption for the configured Marketo subscription (date, total calls_today, per-API-user breakdown), and return {job_id, status} in milliseconds; poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished result. Compare the finished job's calls_today with the operator-confirmed subscription quota before starting a large batch; this verb reports consumption and does not assume the account's quota limit.
embedding_description: Dispatch a background job that reads the configured Marketo subscription's current-day REST API call consumption -- subscription-wide total plus per-user breakdown -- returning a job_id in milliseconds. Poll check_marketo_job_status with that job_id for the finished usage data. Use to budget a large batch or check remaining daily quota headroom before a bulk read or write.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Marketo API usage read job dispatched
result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with job_id (pass to check_marketo_job_status to retrieve the finished usage data) and status (always 'queued' -- this verb never waits for the vendor call).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Confirm the job was dispatched and give the job_id; tell the caller to poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished usage data (date, calls_today, users). Do not claim any usage numbers from THIS verb's response -- it never carries them.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validate the request and dispatch a background job to read the configured Marketo subscription's current-day API usage. This verb only validates and dispatches -- it never talks to Marketo directly.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: This is a DISPATCH-time error only -- caught before any vendor call is made, so no job was created. marketo.invalid_params: session_id/flow_id were missing from the calling context. Vendor-side faults (marketo.auth_failed, marketo.permission_denied, marketo.rate_limited, marketo.daily_quota_exceeded) can NOT surface here -- they only appear later, in check_marketo_job_status's error field, once the background worker actually calls Marketo.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Once dispatch succeeds, poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) -- if THAT reports an error: marketo.permission_denied means the API user's Access API role cannot read subscription usage; marketo.rate_limited means retry after the rate window; marketo.daily_quota_exceeded means stop the batch and wait for the subscription quota reset.
